# rasuvaeff/understudy-psalm

Psalm plugin for `rasuvaeff/understudy`.

## Install

```bash
composer require --dev rasuvaeff/understudy-psalm
vendor/bin/psalm-plugin enable rasuvaeff/understudy-psalm
```

Namespace: `Rasuvaeff\Understudy\Psalm`. Requires PHP 8.3 - 8.5 and
`vimeo/psalm ^6.16`.

## API

- `Rasuvaeff\Understudy\Psalm\Plugin` — the entry point, registered through `extra.psalm.pluginClass`.
- `Rasuvaeff\Understudy\Psalm\Issue\UnderstudyMisuse` — the issue every diagnostic is reported as.

Everything else the plugin registers is `@internal`.

## Rules

- The plugin exists because `Arg::*()` is declared `mixed`: a matcher has to
  be passable wherever a contract declares anything at all. Inside a
  specification closure that is correct and Psalm cannot know it.
- Suppression is narrow by construction. Three things must hold: the issue is
  argument-shaped, its location is inside a call-closure verb — `when()`,
  `expect()`, `expectSequence()`, `verify()` as free functions or on
  `Understudy::`, plus `calls()`, `lastCall()` and `verifySequence()`, which
  exist only there — and its file
  offsets fall inside a call the resolver said is ours — `Rasuvaeff\Understudy\Arg`,
  or a `Captor::capture()` whose receiver Psalm resolved when asked for the
  method's return type. A foreign class named `Arg`, and anybody else's
  `capture()`, keep their diagnostics; ours under an alias loses them.
- A matcher passed to a REAL call is still reported -- BY PSALM, and only at
  `errorLevel="1"`, where its own `MixedArgument` lives. This plugin
  suppresses inside a specification and reports nothing of its own here; at
  level 2 and above a leaked matcher draws nothing until the runtime
  `MatcherLeaked`. `understudy-phpstan` has `understudy.matcherLeak` and
  reports at every level; the deliberate difference is that a textual leak
  rule also misreads a matcher reaching its specification through a variable,
  a property or a helper.
- `Arg::rest()` legitimately passes fewer arguments than the
  contract declares: `TooFewArguments` goes quiet only when the call is
  inside a specification AND its last written argument is `Arg::rest()`. A
  real call ending in `Arg::rest()` keeps both reports.
- `$captor->capture()` (`Arg::captor()`) is a matcher too:
  its argument report goes quiet inside a specification, it does not count
  against "exactly one call per closure", and a leaked capture is reported.
- No baseline, no `@psalm-suppress`. If a diagnostic cannot be expressed
  through public Psalm hooks it is dropped from the plan rather than faked.

## What it reports

- `UnderstudyMisuse` — a matcher whose kind the parameter can never accept; a
  closure specifying nothing, two calls, or a static method; cardinality no
  run can satisfy; contradictory `verify()` arguments.
- Psalm's own `InvalidArgument` on `returns()` and `answers()`. The plugin
  does not check those: it fills in the builder's template parameter from the
  method being specified, and `WhenBuilder<TReturn>` already declares
  `returns(TReturn ...)`, so Psalm checks them itself.
- Psalm's own `InvalidArrayOffset` and method diagnostics on `wire()`, whose
  shape is read from the named class's constructor. An intersection parameter
  keeps its intersection — the core builds one double for all of it. A union
  naming two object types makes the core refuse the class (`CannotWire`), so
  no shape is produced for that call at all. A dynamic class-string is left
  alone.
